pool.title: Direct HTTP Dispatch For Zero-Tool Seats
pool.body: In measured Lite runs, ballot votes consumed roughly 193,000 tokens across three calls because host subagent wrappers add over 60,000 tokens of startup context per 2,000-token packet. Yet protocol logic in src/run/dispatch.rs already marks vote, rank, control, and elder phases as needing zero tools. Whenever an OpenRouter key or compatible HTTP endpoint is configured, council dispatch should route all zero-tool seats directly through providers::openrouter via the existing ureq client instead of spawning external subagent processes. Bypassing subagent instantiation preserves strict timeout envelopes, isolation, and clean JSON completions while eliminating over eighty percent of ballot and elder token spend with zero new crate dependencies.
pool.eli5: Route tool-free vote, elder, and control seats through direct HTTP calls instead of heavy subagents.

pool.title: Minimalist Dynamic MCP Toolset Gating
pool.body: The MCP server currently advertises between 22 and 27 tools on tools/list, outputting 19 to 23 kilobytes of comprehensive JSON schemas. When an AI host initializes or interacts with the server, these exhaustive schemas are injected directly into context, consuming several thousand prompt tokens on every turn. The server should default to a compact core toolset containing only primary workflow operations such as init, next, ingest, status, cut, and note. Specialized administrative tools like blind verification, memory reconfiguration, and lock inspection should remain tucked behind an explicit flag or progressive disclosure. This reduces baseline MCP token consumption without removing any functionality.
pool.eli5: Default MCP tools list to a compact six-tool core, cutting massive schema bloat on every host prompt.

pool.title: Static Policy Slug Mapping And Dual Hook Ingestion
pool.body: Current cross-lab dispatch defaults to stand-ins because models/lock.yaml lacks OpenRouter slugs unless an online refresh was executed, while src/providers.rs only checks raw environment variables. Adding a static slug table in models/policy.yaml gives deterministic cross-lab model resolution offline. Concurrently, src/hook.rs fails on Antigravity IDE events because it only parses snake_case tool_name and tool_input fields from Claude Code instead of camelCase toolCall structures. Extending the hook payload parser to accept both JSON schemas enables seamless IDE integration without proxy wrappers, ensuring that cross-lab seats and automated hooks execute reliably across heterogeneous client environments without touching external crates.
pool.eli5: Add static provider slugs in policy.yaml and support camelCase IDE hook payloads to ensure reliable multi-client dispatch.

pool.title: Resilient hook parsing and Windows case-insensitive locking
pool.body: The pre-tool hook in src/hook.rs expects Claude Code payload keys such as tool_name and tool_input. When executed inside other agent harnesses like Antigravity, payloads provide camelCase fields like toolName or nested toolCall objects, causing the hook to see empty strings and silently permit edits to locked test files. Furthermore, path lookups in locked sets rely on case-sensitive set containment, failing on Windows where filesystems ignore letter casing. By normalizing incoming JSON event keys across snake_case and camelCase variants and applying case-insensitive relative path normalization on Windows platforms, the hook guarantees tamper-proof test locking and seat lane boundaries everywhere.
pool.eli5: Make hooks parse both camelCase and snake_case while matching Windows paths case-insensitively to prevent security bypasses.

pool.title: Resilient ballot parsing and qualified leak detection
pool.body: Strict validation in src/run/validate.rs and src/core.rs triggers costly seat respawns over harmless formatting slips. In src/core.rs, label parsing requires exact string boundaries, discarding valid ballots containing markdown bolding or candidate title annotations. Meanwhile, identity leak checks match unqualified two-letter tokens, spuriously flagging standard engineering acronyms and forcing hundred-thousand-token seat retries. Relaxing label extraction to capture leading candidate letters across markdown styles and restricting leak patterns to qualified role references preserves protocol integrity while preventing spurious validation rejections. This drastically cuts wasted startup tokens and unnecessary provider retries across all seats without lowering council evaluation standards.
pool.eli5: Allow markdown in ballots and qualify leak checks to prevent expensive validation failures and seat respawns.
